meta.guide_tau: Level caption:  energy (NIST, or a measurement of the last 20 years where one exists) and measured lifetime (where one exists).
meta.notes: Conventions. (1) Isotope-shift keys 'a-b' mean nu(a) - nu(b); the 253.7 nm and 313 nm shifts are relative to 198Hg as printed. 199Hg / 201Hg shifts of the 253.7 nm line are hyperfine centres of gravity corrected by Schelfhout & McFerran for the second-order hyperfine interaction. (2) Clock frequencies exceed double precision: use value_Hz_str / unc_Hz. frequency_THz_<A> carries further isotopes. (3) Fields beyond SCHEMA.md: natural_linewidth_*, hyperfine_component_frequencies, frequency_ratios, magic_frequency_MHz, g_factor_<A>Hg (g of the J=0 clock state, x1 not x1e3), top-level 'rydberg' (ionization limit) and 'conflicts'. (4) A_s, linewidth and rme_J_ea0 of the 253.7 nm line are derived here from the measured lifetime (schema convention, single decay channel). (5) Only the 201Hg magnetic hyperfine constants could be sourced; the 199Hg values are missing (see not_found).

levels.tau_src: Porsev, Safronova, Safronova, 'A theoretical study of the g-factor and lifetime of the 6s6p 3P0 state of mercury', Phys. Rev. A 96, 012509 (2017), arXiv:1703.01349. Note: derived: 1/A with the measured 199Hg hyperfine-quenching rate A(3P0->1S0) = 0.692(14) s^-1 of Wexler, Wilcomb, Djeu, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 70, 863 (1980), as quoted by Porsev et al. (original not opened). 199Hg only; bosonic isotopes have no single-photon decay at B=0.

levels.name: 5d^{10}6s7s\ ^3S_{1}
levels.tau_src: Mosburg & Wilke, 'Some new transition probabilities for mercury I', J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 19, 69 (1978). Note: measured lifetime as tabulated in Mosburg & Wilke Table 1; original: Holt & Pipkin, Phys. Rev. A 9, 581 (1974), cascade coincidence. Mosburg & Wilke adopt the average 8.3 ns (A_tot = 1.20e8 s^-1). The NIST ASD A values of the four decay lines sum to 1.26e8 s^-1 (7.9 ns, derived).
